title: Patient behavior and communication words
blurb: Describe how a patient acts, feels and communicates in HESI A2 words, and keep compliant, complacent, apathy and empathy apart.
question: A shift note says one patient is noncompliant and belligerent, another is withdrawn and shows apathy, and a third is adamant about refusing surgery. What is each patient actually doing?

teach.h: Words for how people act and talk
teach.body: Formally, behavior and communication words describe a person's cooperation with care, mood, attitude and rights in the care relationship. In plain English: is the patient following the plan, how are they acting, how do they feel, and what may they decide? These are everyday English words that appear constantly in health settings, so the HESI A2 tests them with look-alike distractors such as compliant and complacent.

teach.caption: Compliant is also not complaint (a noun: an expression of unhappiness).

Volatile means likely to change suddenly: a volatile patient can jump along this scale.

teach.h: Scenario: Sofia reads a shift report
teach.body: Sofia Nguyen, a medical assistant applying to an LPN program, reads: 'Room 4: candid about drinking, reluctant to abstain. Room 6: adamant about going home; autonomy respected. Room 9: agitated at night, docile by morning.' She translates: Room 4 is honest about alcohol but hesitant to give it up. Room 6 will not change her mind, and the team accepts her right to decide. Room 9 is restless at night and calm by morning.

teach.caption: Defer has two senses: the sentence decides. 'Defer until May' = postpone; 'defer to the doctor' = yield.

teach.text: Look-alike sets the HESI A2 uses: compliant / complacent / complaint; apathy / empathy / antipathy; adamant (will not budge) vs ambivalent (torn both ways); confidential (private) vs confident (sure); rapport (trust) vs report (account). And never pick the option that simply fits the story: a belligerent visitor may also be confused, but belligerent means hostile.

items: Compliant = follows the plan; noncompliant = does not; adhere = follow closely; abstain = go without.
Apathy = no interest; empathy = shares feelings; antipathy = strong dislike.
Docile calm, withdrawn quiet, irritable easily annoyed, agitated restless, belligerent hostile, volatile changeable.
Reluctant = unwilling; adamant = unyielding; candid = frank; impaired = weakened.
Consent = permission; confidential = private; disclose = reveal; autonomy = self-determination; rapport = trust.

summary: You can now describe a patient's cooperation, mood, attitude and rights using exact HESI A2 words. You can also separate the look-alike sets that become distractors: compliant and complacent, apathy and empathy, adamant and ambivalent, defer and differ.

A.q: Which word means "not following a prescribed plan or instructions"?
A.why: Noncompliant means not following a prescribed plan or instructions (non- = not, compliant = following).

whyNot.0: Noncommittal means not revealing an opinion or decision.
whyNot.2: Nonchalant means calm and casual, unconcerned.
whyNot.3: Incompetent means lacking the ability to do something.

A.q: The patient became combative when the aide reached for his arm to take his blood pressure. What is the best definition of the word "combative" in this sentence?
A.why: Combative means ready or eager to fight or argue.

whyNot.0: Willing to cooperate is the opposite of combative.
whyNot.1: Weakness fits a hospital patient loosely, but combative describes hostility.
whyNot.3: Confusion may cause the behavior, but it is not the meaning of combative.

A.q: Mrs. Grey has been withdrawn since she moved into the nursing home. What is the best definition of the word "withdrawn" in this sentence?
A.why: Withdrawn means quiet and not wanting to interact with others.

whyNot.0: Angry and demanding is the opposite of quiet withdrawal.
whyNot.2: Wasting away is withered, a look-alike word.
whyNot.3: Nighttime confusion is a different sign.

B.q: Before the operation, Mr. Dunn signed a form giving his consent. What is the best definition of the word "consent" in this sentence?
B.why: Consent is permission or agreement: the form records his permission for the operation.

whyNot.0: A history form is common before surgery, but consent means permission.
whyNot.2: Insurance details fit a form loosely, but they are not consent.
whyNot.3: An emergency contact is another form field, not the meaning of consent.

B.q: All patient records on this unit are confidential. What is the best definition of the word "confidential" in this sentence?
B.why: Confidential means intended to be kept private.

whyNot.0: Storage method fits records loosely, but confidential is about privacy.
whyNot.1: Authorship is not the meaning of confidential.
whyNot.2: Accuracy is about correctness, not privacy.

B.q: Ms. Park finally disclosed that she had stopped taking her heart medication. What is the best definition of the word "disclosed" in this sentence?
B.why: Disclose means to make known or reveal.

whyNot.1: Denied is the opposite of disclosed.
whyNot.2: She may regret it, but disclosed means she told someone.
whyNot.3: Deciding to stop is the earlier choice; disclosed means making it known.

C.q: The new resident deferred to the attending physician's judgment on the treatment plan. What is the best definition of the word "deferred" in this sentence?
C.why: In 'deferred to someone's judgment,' defer means to give way to another's judgment.

whyNot.0: Disagreeing is differ, a look-alike word and the opposite idea.
whyNot.2: Making reference is refer, a sound-alike.
whyNot.3: Reporting fits a hospital setting loosely, but it is not the meaning of defer.

C.q: A stroke left Mr. Burke with impaired speech, so he uses a picture board to communicate. What is the best definition of the word "impaired" in this sentence?
C.why: Impaired means weakened or damaged in function.

whyNot.0: Fully recovered is the opposite; he still needs a picture board.
whyNot.1: Quiet speech is low volume, not damaged function.
whyNot.3: Repetition is not the meaning of impaired.

C.q: The hospital's patient advocate helped Mrs. Ruiz file a complaint about her bill. What is the best definition of the word "advocate" in this sentence?
C.why: An advocate is a person who speaks for or supports another.

whyNot.0: An opponent is an adversary, the opposite role.
whyNot.1: A billing clerk fits the topic loosely, but an advocate supports the patient.
whyNot.3: A judge stays neutral; an advocate takes the patient's side.

reteach.title: Behavior words on a sports team
reteach.question: Think of players on a team and how they respond to the coach. Which player matches each behavior word?

blocks.body: The compliant player runs every drill the coach sets. The noncompliant player skips them. The complacent player thinks the team is too good to lose and stops trying. The reluctant player goes along but drags their feet. The adamant player refuses to change positions, no matter what. The captain who speaks up for a benched teammate is an advocate.

blocks.text: Compliant and complacent sound alike, but the compliant player follows the plan while the complacent player stops caring about it.

explain.body: Compliant = follows instructions. Noncompliant = does not. Adhere = follow closely. Abstain = choose not to have something. Complacent = smug and careless.

test.q: Which word means "following instructions or rules as required"?
test.why: Compliant means following instructions or rules as required.

whyNot.0: Complacent means self-satisfied and unaware of possible danger.
whyNot.1: Competent means having the skill to do something well.
whyNot.3: Complicit means involved with others in wrongdoing.

explain.body: Apathy = no interest or concern. Empathy = understanding another's feelings. Antipathy = strong dislike. All share path, meaning feeling.

test.q: Which word means "lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern"?
test.why: Apathy is a lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern (a- = without).

whyNot.1: Empathy is understanding and sharing another's feelings.
whyNot.2: Antipathy is strong dislike, which is a strong feeling, not a lack of one.
whyNot.3: Sympathy is feeling sorry for another's trouble.

explain.body: Docile = calm. Withdrawn = quiet, avoids others. Irritable = easily annoyed. Agitated = nervous, restless. Belligerent and combative = hostile. Volatile = changes suddenly.

test.q: Which word means "easily annoyed or made angry"?
test.why: Irritable means easily annoyed or made angry.

whyNot.0: Docile means calm and easily managed, the opposite.

explain.body: Consent = permission. Confidential = private. Disclose = reveal. Autonomy = the right to decide for oneself. Advocate = speaks for another. Rapport = a relationship of trust.

test.q: The nurse built rapport with the frightened teenager by asking about his favorite team. What is the best definition of the word "rapport" in this sentence?
test.why: Rapport is a relationship of trust and mutual understanding.

whyNot.0: A written account is a report, the sound-alike.
whyNot.2: Rules are not the meaning of rapport.
whyNot.3: Asking about interests builds rapport, but a list of interests is not rapport.
